property_summary: The reference supportsInterface returns true only for the IAccessControl interface ID, while the buggy version returns true for any interface ID; therefore for a fuzzed interfaceId that does not equal type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, the reference returns false but the buggy version returns true.
For any interfaceId not equal to type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, the reference's supportsInterface returns false, but the buggy version returns true.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true only if the contract supports that interface; the reference returns true for IAccessControl and IERC165, but the buggy version returns true for all interfaceIds, breaking this rule.

For any interfaceId that is not type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, the reference returns false but the buggy version returns true, so supportsInterface must not return true for an unsupported interface.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true exactly when the contract supports that interface; the reference returns true only for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId and type(IERC165).interfaceId, but the buggy version returns true for all interfaceIds, so for any non-supported interfaceId the reference returns false while the bug returns true.
supportsInterface(type(IAccessControl).interfaceId) must return true in the correct contract, but the mutant always returns false.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return true if and only if interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId; the mutant always returns false, violating this for those IDs.

For any input, supportsInterface must return false for an interfaceId that is neither type(IERC165).interfaceId nor type(IAccessControl).interfaceId; the reference does, but the mutant also returns false, so there is no difference — however, the bug actually breaks the rule that supportsInterface must return true for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, which the reference returns true for.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true if and only if it is type(IERC165).interfaceId or type(IAccessControl).interfaceId; the mutant returns false for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface(interfaceId) must equal (interfaceId == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId) || (interfaceId == type(IERC165).interfaceId); the mutant always returns false, violating this for both type(IAccessControl).interfaceId and type(IERC165).interfaceId.

The correct implementation returns true for both IAccessControl and IERC165 interface IDs, while the buggy implementation only returns true for IAccessControl and false for IERC165, violating ERC165 interface discovery.

For any interfaceId, if the reference contract returns true for supportsInterface(interfaceId), the mutant must also return true; the mutant breaks this by returning false for type(IERC165).interfaceId, which the reference accepts.
The reference contract returns true for type(IERC165).interfaceId because of the super call chain, but the mutant returns false for that interface ID, breaking ERC165 compliance.

For any interfaceId, if the reference supportsInterface returns true, the mutant must also return true; the mutant breaks this by returning false for type(IERC165).interfaceId while the reference returns true.
For any role and account, if _grantRole is called to assign the role to the account, hasRole must return true afterwards; the buggy version breaks this by always returning false.
For any role and account, the result of hasRole must equal the membership stored in the contract; the buggy version always returns false, so the equality fails whenever the account has the role.

For any role R and account A, c.hasRole(R, A) must return true if A was granted R and the role has not been revoked; the mutant always returns false, so it returns false when the role was previously granted.
For any role and account, after a call to _grantRole(role, account), the return value of hasRole(role, account) must be true; the mutant always returns false, violating this rule.
If an account is granted a role and that role is never revoked, hasRole(role, account) must return true; the mutant always returns false, breaking this for the granted account.
For any role and account, hasRole must return the actual membership status; the mutant inverts the result, so when membership is true the mutant returns false and vice versa.

For any role and account, hasRole returns the same value as _roles[role].members[account]; the mutant inverts the boolean, so the return always equals zero for true membership and one for false membership.

For any role and any account, hasRole returns true if and only if the internal membership is true; the mutant inverts the result, so the return value equals the negation of the membership, and an admin who has been granted the default admin role will always see a different return value.
If a function pointer (role) is set to the DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE and an account is granted that role, then calling hasRole with that role and account must return true, but the mutant returns false.

For any role and any account, hasRole returns the same boolean as _roles[role].members[account] (which can be read via a secondary role setup); since the mutant negates the return, a granted role will show inconsistent membership across independent checks.
For any role and account, if that role is granted to that account, hasRole must return true; the buggy version always returns false regardless of role membership.
For any input, hasRole must return true if and only if the role was previously granted; the buggy always returns false, so for a previously granted role it disagrees with the reference.
For any role and account where a role has been granted, the reference hasRole returns true; the buggy hasRole always returns false, so for any granted role it disagrees.

For any role/account pair where the role exists in _roles and hasRole returns true in the reference, the buggy version returns false; more precisely, after granting PROPOSER_ROLE to an account, the reference hasRole returns true on that pairing while the buggy always returns false.

For any role, getRoleAdmin returns the actual admin role, never DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE unless the admin was explicitly set to 0x00. The bug always returns DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE even for roles with a different admin.
